correctness.rationale: For any strict source relation x<u, the height-two hypothesis places x on the lower side and u on the upper side. Replacing lower-side values in the top two target levels by a fixed point of level h-2 gives an order-preserving f1<=f. Then every lower endpoint has level at most h-2, so replacing top-level upper-side values by a fixed point of level h-1 gives order-preserving f2<=f1. Since f2 avoids the top level, f2 is pointwise below a top-level constant. Comparable finite-space maps are homotopic, yielding f~constant. The height-two target counterexample follows from H1 of the four-point crown. The checker exhaustively verified 18,598 small maps but is supplementary to the proof.

value.rationale: The theorem is a sharp structural boundary across an entire natural source class. It shows that the incidence pattern of every finite height-two source becomes irrelevant to direct finite-space homotopy once a weak-order target has a third level, with an explicit three-comparison witness. The failure at two levels makes the threshold mathematically motivated rather than an arbitrary slice.
